Attach census geography to the addresses it actually describes

Source: R/md-ingest-geocode.R
md_ingest_geocode.Rd

metadata-address-geocoded carries census geography - county, CBSA, tract, block, urban area - plus coordinates, for 3,436,984 EINs.

Usage

md_ingest_geocode(con = NULL, path = NULL, version = "2026-08")

Arguments

con

A connection from md_db().

path

Path to the geocoded CSV.

version

Pinned address_geocoded version.

Value

Row counts, invisibly.

It is one geocode per EIN, not one per address spell

Each row carries a single ORG_ADDR_FULL and the ORG_FISCAL_YEAR it came from, and those years run from 1989 to 2024: 62% are 2020 or later, but 332,621 predate 2000. So the file does not describe "where this organisation is" - it describes where it was in one particular year.

Attaching it to whichever address row happens to be current would therefore be wrong for a third of the file. Instead the geocode is joined back to the address it names, by parsing ORG_ADDR_FULL and matching on (ein, street, city, state, zip5). Rows that match get the geography; rows that do not are reported and dropped. An unattached geocode is better than one attached to the wrong address.

Parsing from the right

ORG_ADDR_FULL is comma-joined street,city,state,zip, and street lines contain commas - "849 ALMAR AVE. STE. C, PMB 217" is a real example from the sibling crosswalk. Splitting left-to-right therefore mis-assigns the fields whenever a street has a comma in it. The last three fields are always city, state and ZIP, so this splits from the right and rejoins whatever remains as the street.

Not all coordinates mean the same thing

ADDR_TYPE records what the geocoder actually resolved, and only 1,783,685 of 3,436,986 rows are PointAddress - an actual rooftop. 693,034 are Postal and 482,890 PostalExt, which are ZIP centroids: a point in the middle of a postal area, not the organisation's location. Treating those as coordinates would put every organisation in a ZIP at the same spot and make any distance-based comparison confidently wrong.

So geocode_type is stored beside the coordinates rather than discarded, and any consumer computing distance should filter on it. The column exists to make that possible; nothing here enforces it.
